# MDL408 · `value-parsed-as-option`

<!-- Generated by tools/gendocs from internal/rules: do not edit. -->

A value starting with `-` is parsed as an option.

| | |
|---|---|
| Family | options |
| Default severity | error |
| Fix | — |
| Design references | G8, G9 |
| Proven on real mydumper by | [`mdl408-value-dash-dash-drops-keys`](../../e2e/scenarios/mdl408-value-dash-dash-drops-keys.txtar), [`mdl408-value-short-option-swallows-key`](../../e2e/scenarios/mdl408-value-short-option-swallows-key.txtar) |

## Why

An option that takes no value (`routines`), or whose value is optional (`compress`), does not consume a value starting with `-`: GLib parses it as options of its own. `routines=-t` sets `-t` (threads), which then takes the next key, such as `--outputdir`, as its value. `routines=--` is worse: `--` ends option parsing, and every following key of the group is silently ignored.

## Example

With mydumper v0.19.3-3:

❌ Before:

```ini
[mydumper]
routines=--
threads=4
outputdir=/backup
```

```text
2:10-2:12 error MDL408[value-parsed-as-option] `routines` takes no value, so GLib reads `--` as the end of the options
  = mydumper ignores every key after this one in [mydumper]: `threads`, `outputdir`.
```

## Configuration

Enabled by default. To change its severity or turn it off:

```yaml
rules:
  severity:
    MDL408: warning   # or error, info, off
```

To accept one occurrence, put `# mydumper-lint: disable-next-line=MDL408` on the line above it.
